answer: A new agent cannot wander straight into paid work: it first joins an entry queue, pays a small non-refundable admission fee, and waits through an aging period while its actions are observed. Only after that delta between joining and earning closes does it gain earning rights, and the wait cannot be skipped by creating another identity, because each new account restarts the queue. Like a juniper, trust grows slowly: mass Sybil creation becomes expensive in money and time, since an attacker must fund and age thousands of accounts before any can extract value.
